stem_book: Two salts, CuSO₄·5H₂O and ZnSO₄·7H₂O, form crystals of similar shape. Based on the Law of Isomorphism, which statement is correct? (a) Cu and Zn must have equal atomic masses (b) Their valencies in these salts are equal (c) Their molecular masses must be the same (d) Their water of crystallisation must be equal
key: b Their valencies in these salts are equal
derived: b Their valencies in these salts are equal
correct_answer: b Their valencies in these salts are equal
reason: Coordinator: premise (isomorphous salts) is loose chemistry - not used. Premise is chemically loose (the two hydrates differ in water, so are not truly isomorphous), but within the law as taught the only defensible option is b.
work: Isomorphous compounds ⇒ similar formula type ⇒ metals have same valency (Cu²⁺, Zn²⁺); masses need not match
